correctness.rationale: The Pólya predictive product gives exchangeability and the positive beta-binomial mass p_{n,r}. Conditional uniform placement of r occurrences of colour one yields exactly 2r(n-r)/n switches against other colours; the remaining (q−1)-colour Pólya draw pair has disagreement probability b. Thus conditional expectation gives covariance q*p*F/n. The coefficient b−d=−a(a+1)/[(qa+1)((q−1)a+1)] is strictly negative, F(r)=−r(r−1)d<0 for r≥2, and F(qr)=r(a+r)(q−1)(qa+2)/[(qa+1)((q−1)a+1)]>0. This establishes two roots and every sign case; singleton factorization gives the unique crossing. Exact enumeration of 186 cases and symbolic simplification of identities and limiting roots passed. Finite checks are corroborative; the all-parameter proof is algebraic.

originality.rationale: The exact joint run-length and colour-count law was established by Eryilmaz (2008); that more general finite distribution can in principle compute any joint moment, so no novelty is claimed for the underlying law. The inspected statements do not furnish the universally strict, all-concentration negative–positive–negative frequency/switch covariance classification, its exact singleton boundary or its linear-in-frequency root locations. The direct comparable iid frequency/collision and reinforced singleton-pair results concern different joint observables; none directly implies these universal sign inequalities. Historical priority remains qualified by the possibility of an unlocated equivalent specialization.
residual_risks: Eryilmaz (2008) derives a broad finite joint run/frequency distribution that mathematically permits summing to the present covariance; novelty is limited to the exact two-root phase classification and its parameter-uniform proof.

value.rationale: The fixed-frequency spectrum of reinforced samples is an interpretable diversity/Good–Turing statistic, while run transitions measure order-dependent clustering. A universal concentration-robust two-transition phase and sharp singleton threshold explain how their dependence can reverse twice even though one is order-invariant and the other order-sensitive. The two roots lie strictly across the natural sample size n=qr for every q,a,r≥2, and have distinct linear asymptotic slopes. That complete structural boundary is not an arbitrary finite computation or a claim for a routine unmotivated normalization; it refines rather than reclaims the known general joint run distribution.
